text:
alex: Hey all — kicking off the RFC thread for the runtime change: adaptive kernel selector + attention fusion paths + KV eviction tweaks. I sketched a short PRD and initial acceptance criteria. Need quick feedback on launch gates, customer asks, and edge cases.

hema: Thanks Alex — can you paste the concrete customer SLOs we need to meet?

alex: ACME (pilot) asks: p99 latency <= 120ms for 2k token chat sessions at steady-state for the Llama2-70B variant, and a nominal goal of -20% cost-per-token versus baseline. We should treat cost reduction as desirable but not blocking if SLOs fail.

li: For rollout: canary at 5% traffic for 24h, 25% for 48h, then 100%. Auto-rollback if errors +5% or p95 latency +15% vs baseline during canary. Thoughts?

sophia: Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Functional parity on top-100 prompt set (no more than 1% drop in exact-match/qa metrics)
- No P99 regressions > 10% absolute (or >15ms, whichever is smaller) for pinned customer workloads
- End-to-end cost-per-token measured across 72h window shows improvement or within -5% of baseline for critical customers
- Canary stability: less than 1% increase in 500/502/504 errors

allen: Edge cases to call out: long prefix reuse (chat sessions with huge KV reuse), multi-tenant cache collisions, and interleaved streaming where fused-attn changes output pacing. Also quantized kernels might show tiny determinism diffs — add evals for flakiness.

alex: Good. Ops asks: add a toggle to force kernel variant per-model. We need tracing hooks to see kernel chosen per-request and a small histogram metric for per-kernel latency and token throughput.

hema: Also add a config example for SRE/SEs to patch quickly. Something like:
```yaml
kernel_policy:
  prefer_fused_attn_above_tokens: 512
  fallback: "quant_kernel_v2"
  cache_eviction: "sticky_lru"
  sticky_prefix_ttl_s: 3600
```

li: About KV eviction: proposal is sticky-LRU that pins long-lived prefixes for X sessions, but we need a memory budget per-tenant and global eviction under memory pressure. Add a hard cap metric and OOM guard.

allen: Test matrix:
- perf bench (1k/2k/4k seq) on pinned models
- regression eval on top-100 prompts + randomized fuzzing for generation divergence
- multi-tenant cache load test (scale to 10k concurrent sessions)

sophia: Quality gates: run automatic eval harness comparing tokens using our eval scoring. If mean ROUGE/BLEU drops by >1.5% on any production prompt bucket, fail the build.

alex: Launch criteria checklist (draft):
- RFC approved by eng-runtime + eng-ml + security
- Canary plan documented + deploy playbook
- Metrics: kernel_choice, kernel_latency_hist, kv_evictions, cache_hit_ratio, memory_pressure, model_quality_score
- Rollback plan and feature toggle in place
- Perf delta table attached to RFC (bench numbers within tolerances)

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy window: 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. Will run at 5% traffic for 24h.

hema: One more customer ask: ability to pin older kernel for a tenant if they see quality diffs. Make sure tenant-level override exists.

li: We should add a tolerance budget for token latency tail — propose 15ms slack at p95 and 20ms at p99 for the canary phase to avoid noisy rollbacks.

allen: Security note: KV cache keys must be scrubbed and never logged. Add a privacy checkbox in PRD.

alex: Great feedback — I'll update the RFC with acceptance criteria, rolling gates, and the test matrix. Will attach perf numbers and model list tomorrow. If anyone has blocking objections to criteria above post here.

hema: No objections from me. :thumbsup:

sophia: Seems reasonable. Adding a QA owner to the RFC would help (assigning to me).

li: assigning rollback owner: li.

alex: Cool — next step: I'll push RFC draft to the docs repo and ping this thread when ready. Thanks!
